text:
Nashville has now won four straight, and this one came from the people the Predators lean on most. Roman Josi, the 25-minute defenseman the club took 38th overall in 2008 out of Bern, set up two of the three goals, and Juuse Saros made 25 saves on 26 shots. The Predators beat St. Louis 3-1 at Bridgestone Arena, avenging nothing but extending a run that already included a 5-2 win over the Blues on Oct. 17.

St. Louis led first. Jimmy Snuggerud scored on a power play at 13:07 of the first, and Steven Stamkos answered on a Nashville power play three minutes later. Ross Colton put the Predators ahead in the second, and Nick Perbix sealed it at 18:31 of the third on a shot our numbers gave only a 5 percent chance of going in. The first period was dead even on chance quality (expected goals, which measures how good the shots were, favored St. Louis 1.01 to 0.98), but Nashville took over from there, 1.19 to 0.70 in the second and 0.78 to 0.56 in the third. Saros, who went 99th overall in 2013 and arrived from HPK, saved about 1.3 goals more than the shots he faced should have allowed. Joel Hofer was solid too, stopping 26 of 28.

Our numbers say Nashville deserved to win 60 percent of the time, meaning that share of simulated replays of every shot ended in a Predators win. So the result matched the play, if not by a wide margin. The Predators now carry a four-game winning streak into their next game. We have nothing in the facts on St. Louis's streak or record, but the Blues have now lost both meetings with Nashville this season, and Nashville did most of its damage when it counted, with Stamkos involved in two goals and Josi in two more.
